title.text: Our Lady of Aranzazu Shrine (San Mateo Church)

title_en.text: Our Lady of Aranzazu Shrine (San Mateo Church)

tagline.text: An 1887 brick church and national shrine of Our Lady of Aranzazu

location.label: Location
location.text: General Luna Avenue (Guitnang Bayan I), San Mateo, Rizal

children.text: This church in the center of San Mateo, Rizal, traces its parish to 1596, and the present building was completed in 1887. It is the only parish in the Philippines dedicated to Our Lady of Aranzazu and was declared a national shrine in 2025.
San Mateo is a town in Rizal province that sits at the northeastern edge of Metro Manila. It lies about
24km
east of Manila and about
11km

north of the provincial capital, Antipolo, and borders Quezon City, Marikina and Rodriguez (Montalban). The church stands in the middle of town on General Luna Avenue in Barangay Guitnang Bayan I. Its formal name is the National Shrine and Parish of Our Lady of Aranzazu, though most people simply call it San Mateo Church.

Its history goes back to 1596. Augustinian friars founded the town and built the first parish church on August 29 of that year, dedicated to St. Matthew the Apostle (San Mateo). The Jesuits took over from the Augustinians on December 6, 1696, and in 1705 the Jesuit priest Juan de Echazabal changed the patron to Our Lady of Aranzazu. A first concrete church was built on the present site in 1715, but the 1863 Manila earthquake destroyed it, and the current building was completed in 1887.

The church was damaged during World War II, in 1942, and again in 1990, and repairs and refurnishing were completed in 1993. It is built of brick and concrete in a modern Romanesque style. The Diocese of Antipolo declared it a diocesan shrine on July 16, 2004, and the Catholic Bishops' Conference of the Philippines is reported to have designated it a national shrine on January 25, 2025, with Cardinal Tagle presiding over the solemn declaration rites on August 22 of the same year. It is the only parish in the Philippines dedicated to Our Lady of Aranzazu and the only sister parish of the Sanctuary of Arantzazu in Spain's Basque Country.

It is not a flashy tourist attraction. But it lets you see everyday worship and major feast days in a place of faith that goes back to the Spanish era, which makes it a good one- to two-hour stop in the eastern suburbs of Manila. The church is a place of prayer and worship, so keep that in mind and observe proper etiquette, especially during Mass.

This is the building completed in 1887 after the 1863 earthquake destroyed the earlier church. Exposed brick walls and a belfry are its signature features, and it is described as modern Romanesque in style. From the street in front, you can take in the facade and the belfry together.

blocks.title: A wide nave with wooden pews

children.text: Inside, a spacious nave is lined with wooden pews, and exposed brick walls and chandeliers complete the interior. A rose-patterned stained glass window sends colored light inside, and the mood changes with the direction of the morning and afternoon sun.

blocks.title: The golden altar and the image of Our Lady of Aranzazu

children.text: The image of Our Lady of Aranzazu is enshrined at the center of a gold-painted wooden altar, surrounded by statues of several saints. Mary is shown standing with the infant Jesus, wearing a crown and a mantle. Many worshippers pray quietly before the image.

blocks.title: Basque Arantzazu and the sister parish

children.text: Devotion to Our Lady of Aranzazu comes from Arantzazu in Oñati, in Spain's Basque Country. The San Mateo parish is described as the only parish in the Philippines dedicated to Our Lady of Aranzazu and the only sister parish of the Sanctuary of Arantzazu.

blocks.title: The history of the image's coronation

children.text: The image received an episcopal coronation from Bishop Gabriel Reyes on November 9, 2013, a canonical coronation was decreed on June 17, 2016, and Cardinal Orlando Quevedo is reported to have performed the coronation on May 31, 2017, on behalf of Pope Francis. These events are key to understanding the shrine's standing.

blocks.title: The September feast and town celebrations

children.text: The feast of Our Lady of Aranzazu is on September 9, and the town's San Mateo Festival (Parada ng Kakanin) is held the same day. September 21 is the town's foundation day, and novena Masses and processions take place around the feast. The area around the church gets very crowded during the festivities.

blocks.title: The old center of San Mateo

children.text: The area along General Luna Avenue, where the church stands, is the old center of the town. Jeepneys, UV Express vans and tricycles gather here among markets and small shops, giving you a look at a day in a Philippine small town. Combining the church visit with a walk through town makes a one- to two-hour outing.

It became a diocesan shrine in 2004 and was raised to a national shrine in 2025. This could mean more pilgrims, so visitor information and events may grow in the future. You can check the latest news on the shrine's Facebook page (AranzazuShrine).

items.title: Half-day plan
items.subtitle: Church visit and a walk through town

children.text: Set out for San Mateo from Cubao (Araneta City) or Quezon City. Depending on traffic, the trip can take
about 1 hour
or longer.
Arrive at the church on General Luna Avenue and first look at the facade and belfry from outside. If Mass is in progress, wait quietly at the entrance.
Take your time looking around the nave and the altar. Look for the image of Our Lady of Aranzazu, the stained glass and the brick walls, and take photos respectfully when no Mass is going on.
Walk through the town in front of the church and have a snack. The parish store is reported to sell shrine-related souvenirs.
On a Sunday, you can attend the English Mass. Check the schedule below and look for the latest announcements.
After lunch, continue toward Antipolo or Marikina, or head back to Manila.
Early-morning and 6 PM weekday Masses draw many worshippers, so they are hard times for sightseeing. If you only want to look around, aim for the gaps between Masses.

items.title: September feast plan
items.subtitle: Joining the feast of Our Lady of Aranzazu

children.text: On the feast day itself, arrive early. In 2025, the feast was reported to have begun with a 6 AM Mass.
Watch the town's San Mateo Festival (Parada ng Kakanin) and the other events. The program changes every year, so check the announcements from the town hall and the shrine.
In 2025, there was a Mass event at 2 PM. The times can differ each year, so check this year's schedule.
End the day with the evening thanksgiving Mass. In 2025, a thanksgiving Mass was held at 6 PM. Traffic home is heavy, so leave yourself plenty of time.
This feast schedule is based on 2025 reports. Check the shrine's Facebook page and town hall announcements for this year's schedule.
San Mateo is about
24km
east of central Manila. From Manila or Makati, the easiest way is usually to take LRT-2 or MRT-3 to Cubao and transfer to a jeepney.
A jeepney route (No. 203) toward Silangan is reported to run from the Araneta City modern jeepney terminal in Cubao. It is listed as operating from 4 AM to 10 PM, with a fare of
for the first

plus about

. This route ends in the Silangan area rather than on General Luna Avenue in front of the church, so check with the driver that it goes toward the church.
From Quezon City, follow Batasan-San Mateo Road. An older source mentions a jeepney fare of about
from Quezon City Hall, so confirm the fare locally.
From the Marikina side, the road runs along J.P. Rizal Street, and jeepneys from the terminals in Silangan to Cubao pass through Fortune in Marikina. Routes differ somewhat from terminal to terminal.
The Cubao–San Mateo stretch is very congested at rush hour. To save time, travel in the early morning or in the middle of the afternoon.
Taxis and Grab can take you to areas bordering Metro Manila. Enter the Aranzazu Shrine on General Luna Avenue as your destination.
Travel time varies a lot with traffic, so check the estimated fare in the app.
San Mateo is served by jeepneys, UV Express vans, buses and tricycles. Jeepneys and UV vans run along General Luna Avenue and Mabini Avenue.
You can explore the area around the church on foot and use a tricycle only for outlying barangays. Fares may need bargaining, so confirm before you ride.

The church can be visited year-round, but the dry season is the most comfortable time for getting around outdoors. San Mateo's annual rainfall is listed at about 1,005mm, with the heaviest rain from June to September and the driest months being January and February. Daytime highs are generally

The feast of Our Lady of Aranzazu (September 9) falls in the middle of the rainy season, so rain is likely, but it is the best time to see the town's celebrations. Bring an umbrella or rain jacket and allow plenty of travel time.

The area around the church looks like many Philippine small towns, with small eateries, bakeries and snack stalls clustered near the jeepney stops. There is no particular restaurant worth singling out, so just eat at a local place you spot in town. A parade of kakanin (rice cakes) is reported during the September festival, so that is the time to try them.

Most lodging is in resorts on the outskirts rather than in town. Places listed include Apolonia Resort Hotel in Maly, Ciudad Christhia Resort in Ampid, Timberland Highlands Resort in Guitnang Bayan II and Green Nature Resort & Leisure Park in Guinayang. Confirm rates and whether they are operating before you book. Since a day trip from Manila is easy, most visitors stay in Manila or Antipolo and come over for the day.

You can see the interior quietly if you avoid Mass times (Sunday Masses are listed at 6 AM, 7:30 AM, 9 AM, 12:30 PM in English, 4:30 PM and 6 PM, among others). Times can change, so check the shrine's Facebook page for the latest announcements.
On weekdays, Mass is listed at 6 AM on Monday, 6 AM and 6 PM from Tuesday to Friday, and 6 AM and 6 PM on Saturday (anticipated Mass). Confirm just before you go.
Worshippers are praying inside, so avoid shorts and sleeveless tops and walk quietly. Refrain from taking photos during Mass.
The parish office numbers are listed as 8570-9220 and 8289-6959, among others. If you are visiting as a group, contact them in advance.
For sightseeing and photos, go on a clear morning, when the light comes through the stained glass well.
Around the September 9 feast and the September 21 foundation day, roads get crowded and some may be closed, so use public transport and watch your belongings.
Jeepney routes and fares change often. Check the Sakay app or Google Maps just before you set out.
You can combine this with the Antipolo Cathedral or Marikina nearby to make a full-day trip.
This is a place of faith where Mass and prayer take place. During Mass, do not move around or speak loudly, and dress modestly.
Mass times and feast events change from year to year. The times in this guide are based on 2025–2026 listings, so check the latest announcements.
Traffic in town is very heavy. Allow plenty of travel time at rush hour and on feast days.
In the San Mateo area, the river is reported to flood often in the rainy season and landslides are frequent in the highlands. Adjust your plans during typhoons or heavy rain.
In crowded jeepneys and festival crowds, watch for pickpockets and keep your phone and wallet in front of you.
Interior photography and drone use may be restricted, so ask staff or worshippers first.
The provincial capital of Rizal, about
11km
south of San Mateo. It is home to the Antipolo Cathedral, a well-known pilgrimage site, which makes it a natural next stop on a pilgrimage route.
Marikina, which borders San Mateo, is a city known for its shoemaking industry. The San Mateo Arch is reported to mark the boundary between the two cities.
Another Marian shrine in the Monterey Hills area of Barangay Silangan. You can get there from town by jeepney and tricycle.
San Mateo is nicknamed the mountain biking capital of the Philippines, and Timberland Heights offers mountain biking and motocross. The ground is soft right after the rainy season, so take care.
